entries.sanskrit:
पञ्चमे जातकं नन्दः सूनोः कृत्वा महोत्सवम् ।

गत्वाथ मथुरां प्राप- वसुदेवागमोत्सवम् ॥

महा-मना उदार-चित्तः ॥१॥
entries.literal_english: In the fifth chapter Nanda performed a great festival for the birth of his son. He then went to Mathurā and received the festival occasioned by Vasudeva’s arrival. The phrase mahā-manāḥ means generous-minded.

entries.sanskrit: नियुते द्वे लक्षे । सप्त-तिल-पर्वतांश् च प्रादात् । कथं-भूतान् । रत्नौघैः रत्न-समूहैः । शातकौम्भाम्बरैः सुवर्ण-रसाक्तैर् अम्बरैश् चावृतान्
entries.literal_english: He gave two niyutas, two hundred thousand, and seven mountains of sesame. The gifts were covered with masses of jewels and with garments saturated with the luster of gold.

entries.sanskrit: द्रव्याणां गो-हिरण्यादीनां मध्ये केषाञ्चिद् दानैर् एव शुद्धिर् यथा तथान्न-दानादि-युक्त-जात-कर्मादि-संस्कारैर् एव गर्भाणां शुद्धिर् इति दर्शयितुं प्रतिनियतानि शोधकानि दृष्टान्तत्वेनोदाहरति, कालेनेति । कालेन भूम्य्-आदि, स्नानेन देहादि, शौचेनामेध्य-लिप्तादि, संस्कारैर् गर्भादि, तपसा इन्द्रियादि, इज्यया ब्राह्मणादि, दानैर् द्रव्यादि, सन्तुष्ट्या मनः, आत्मा आत्म-विद्यया इति ।
word_for_word: the self by knowledge of the self
entries.literal_english: To show that certain purifying means are prescribed for particular things, Śrīdhara gives examples. Time purifies the earth and similar things; bathing purifies the body; cleanliness purifies what has been smeared with impurity; saṃskāras purify the embryo; austerity purifies the senses; sacrifice purifies the brāhmaṇas; gifts purify wealth; satisfaction purifies the mind; and self-knowledge purifies the self.

entries.sanskrit: सौमङ्गल्य-गिरः स्वस्ति-वाचका विप्रादयो बभूवुः । तत्र, "सूताः पौराणिकाः प्रोक्ता मागधा वंश-शंसकाः बन्दिनस् त्व् अमल-प्रज्ञाः प्रस्ताव-सदृशोक्तयः ।"
entries.literal_english: The brāhmaṇas and others uttered auspicious words and blessings. Sūtas are reciters, Paurāṇikas are narrators of the Purāṇas, Māgadhas praise lineages, and Bandins, whose understanding is pure, speak words suitable to a formal introductory address.

entries.sanskrit: संमृष्टानि संसिक्तानि च द्वाराण्य् अजिराण्य् अङ्गनानि गृहान्तराणि गृह-मध्यानि च यस्मिन् स तथा । चित्र-ध्वजेषु पताकानां स्रजश् च चैल-पल्लव-तोरणानि च तैर् भूषिताः ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: The gates, courtyards, yards, inner rooms and central spaces were swept and sprinkled. The place was decorated with colorful flags, garlands, cloth and leaf festoons and gateways.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: हरिद्रा-तैलै रूषिता लिप्ताः । विचित्र-धातवश् च बर्ह-स्रजश् च वस्त्राणि च काञ्चन-मालाश् चालङ्कारतया विद्यन्ते तेषां ते । तथा-भूता गवादयो बभूवुर् इत्य् अर्थः ।
entries.literal_english: The cows and the other animals had been smeared with turmeric and oil. They were adorned with variegated minerals, peacock-feather garlands, garments and golden necklaces; this is the meaning of the description.

entries.sanskrit: नव-कुङ्कुम-किञ्जल्कैर् मुख-पङ्कजेषु भूतिः श्रीर् यषां ताः ।
entries.literal_english: Their lotus-like faces were beautified by the fresh filaments of saffron.

entries.sanskrit: हरेर् निवासेन ये आत्मनि गुणाः सर्व-प्रियत्वादयस् तैः । रमाया आक्रीडं विहार-स्थानम् ॥१८॥
word_for_word: such as being dear to all
entries.literal_english: Because Hari resides there, the qualities present in the self—such as being beloved by everyone—are present there. It is the playground, the place of Rāma’s pastimes.

entries.sanskrit: भ्रातरं सखायम् । तद् अवमोचनं तस्य नन्दस्य वसति-स्थानम् ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: A brother and a friend. Its release from that condition is the dwelling-place of that Nanda.

entries.sanskrit: पुनर्-भवः पुनर्-जात इव । तत्र हेतु-गर्भं विशेषणं संसार-चक्रे वर्तमान इति ॥२४॥
entries.literal_english: Rebirth, as though one has been born again. The adjective ‘moving within the wheel of saṃsāra’ supplies the reason.

entries.sanskrit: दुर्लभत्वम् एवाह---नैकत्रेति । प्रियश् चासौ संवासश् च प्रिय-संवासः । हे प्रियेति वा । स्रोतस ओघेन नीयमानानां प्लवन्तीति प्लवास् तृणकाष्टादयस् तेषां यथैकत्र स्थितिर् नास्ति तद्वत् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: by the flood of a current
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara explains the rarity of such companionship: a beloved shared residence, or the address ‘O dear one,’ is meant. Just as pieces of grass and wood carried along by a current do not remain together in one place, so living beings carried by the stream of existence do not remain together.

entries.sanskrit: कच्चिद् इति । पशव्यादि-रूपे तस्मिन् वने निर्दोष-गोपयोदध्य्-आदि-प्रभूत-गोपिकास् तन्यादिना पुत्र-क्षेम-विवक्षया पृच्छति, प्रसक्त-धिः स्वात्म-जयोर् इत्य् उक्तवात्
word_for_word: abundant in yogurt and so on
with the welfare of sons intended
to his own self and son
entries.literal_english: In that forest, in its animal and other forms, he asks about the faultless cowherd women, abundant in yogurt and other dairy products, with the welfare of their sons in mind. His mind is attached to his own self and to his son, as the preceding statement indicates.

entries.sanskrit: पुत्रादर्शन-क्लेशान् आह---पुंस इति । सुहृदो बन्धून् प्रत्य् अनुभावितः संपादितो यस् त्रि-वर्गः स हि पुंसो विहितो युक्तः शास्त्रेण वा प्रोक्तो न स्व-मात्र-पर्यवसितः । अतस् तेषु क्लिश्यमानेषु सुखाय न भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥
entries.literal_english: Nanda speaks of the pain caused by not seeing the sons. The three aims of life produced through friends and relatives are appropriate to a person, being enjoined by scripture and not ending in the person alone. Therefore, when those dear ones suffer, those aims do not bring happiness.

entries.sanskrit: अदृष्टे एव निष्ठा समाप्तिर् यस्य सः । यदैव पुत्रादि-सुख-प्रदम् अदृष्टं हीयते तदैव ते पुत्रादयो न भवन्तीत्य् अर्थः । अदृष्ट-परमः तथा अदृष्टम् एव परमं यस्य सः । यद्य् अपि पुत्रादयो वियुक्तास् तथापि तान् अदृष्टम् एव पुनः सङ्गमयतीत्य् अर्थः । एवम् अदृष्टम् आत्मनस् तत्त्वम् अव्यभिचारि-कारणं सुख-दुःखयोर् यो वेद स न मुह्यति । तस्माद् इदानीं त्वया न दुःखं भवनीयम् । मृतानाम् अपि वियुक्तानाम् अपि च कालान्तरे दर्शन-योगयोः सम्भवात् । अस्मद् आदिभिर् अपि कालान्तरे तद्-वियोगे सत्य् अपीति नन्दस्य दैवी वाग् एषा भावि-सूचिक ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: The unseen result is the only foundation, the thing whose completion rests solely on the unseen. When the unseen that gives happiness through sons and other relationships declines, those sons and others are no longer present. The unseen is supreme: it alone is the supreme cause. Even when sons and others are separated, the unseen brings them together again. One who knows the unseen as the unfailing cause of happiness and sorrow is not bewildered. Therefore you should not grieve now, since the dead and the separated may be seen and joined again after some time. Nanda’s words are a divine utterance that points toward what will come.

entries.sanskrit: तां बुद्ध्वा वसुदेवो दुःखं त्यक्त्वा नन्दम् आह---करो वै इति । वो युष्माभिः ॥३१॥
entries.literal_english: Understanding this, Vasudeva gives up his grief and speaks to Nanda: ‘You indeed…’ The word vo means ‘by you’ or ‘by all of you.’
